categories.title: Scope & inventory
categories.lead: Start with a known hostname, network or organisation. Cross-check ownership before treating a match as your asset.

templates.title: Hostname footprint
templates.note: Find banners associated with matching hostnames.
templates.tip: A hostname match is a lead, not verified ownership.

templates.title: Network inventory
templates.note: List indexed services in the chosen CIDR range.
templates.tip: Confirm the network belongs in your assessment scope.

templates.title: Organisation label
templates.note: Match Shodan’s organisation metadata.
templates.tip: Hosting-provider labels can cover unrelated tenants.

templates.title: Autonomous system
templates.note: Search services attributed to an ASN.
templates.tip: An ASN may include customers and shared infrastructure.

templates.title: One port in your network
templates.note: Narrow an inventory to a selected port.
templates.tip: Inspect the banner to identify the actual protocol.

templates.title: Hostname with organisation
templates.note: Require both a hostname and organisation match.
templates.tip: If results disappear, check each filter independently.

categories.title: Web services
categories.lead: Explore page metadata and web-service fingerprints without sending a request to the target from this app.

templates.title: Standard web ports
templates.note: Look for indexed services on common web ports.
templates.tip: Comma-separated values are alternatives within this filter.

templates.title: Additional web ports
templates.note: Review services on common alternate web ports.
templates.tip: Port numbers alone do not establish the service type.

templates.title: Login page titles
templates.note: Find pages whose title mentions login.
templates.tip: A login page does not itself establish an exposure.

templates.title: Successful HTTP responses
templates.note: Find indexed pages with HTTP status 200.
templates.tip: The recorded response may differ from the current page.

templates.title: HTTP redirects
templates.note: Find recorded redirect responses.
templates.tip: Review the destination and whether the redirect is expected.

templates.title: Organisation mentioned in HTML
templates.note: Match an organisation name within captured HTML.
templates.tip: Text matches can include third-party content.

categories.title: TLS & certificates
categories.lead: Compare certificate and protocol observations. These are indexed observations, not a live TLS assessment.

templates.title: Services with TLS data
templates.note: Find results carrying TLS information.
templates.tip: Inspect the certificate and scan timestamp.

templates.title: Expired certificates
templates.note: Find certificates marked expired in the indexed data.
templates.tip: Confirm the endpoint still serves the same certificate.

templates.title: TLS 1.3 support
templates.note: Find recorded support for TLS 1.3.
templates.tip: One supported version does not describe the entire TLS policy.

templates.title: Legacy TLS 1.0 support
templates.note: Review endpoints observed supporting TLS 1.0.
templates.tip: Use an authorised current check before reporting a finding.

templates.title: Certificate common-name pivot
templates.note: Search certificate subject common names.
templates.tip: Certificate names can be stale, shared or unrelated to ownership.

templates.title: HTTP/2 negotiation
templates.note: Find TLS services advertising HTTP/2 through ALPN.
templates.tip: ALPN describes protocol negotiation, not application security.

categories.title: Remote access & management
categories.lead: Review expected remote-access entry points within a network you manage.

templates.title: SSH candidates
templates.note: Find services recorded on port 22.
templates.tip: Check the service banner before classifying them as SSH.

templates.title: SSH outside the usual port
templates.note: Find SSH-related banners away from port 22.
templates.tip: Compare the result with your approved access paths.

templates.title: Remote Desktop candidates
templates.note: Review services on the usual RDP port.
templates.tip: Check whether access is intended to be internet-reachable.

templates.title: VNC candidates
templates.note: Review common VNC listener ports.
templates.tip: A port match does not establish authentication status.

templates.title: Telnet candidates
templates.note: Review services recorded on port 23.
templates.tip: Verify the protocol and whether plaintext access is intended.

templates.title: Selected management port
templates.note: Inspect a particular port across matching hostnames.
templates.tip: Use the observed product and timestamp to triage results.

categories.title: Software fingerprints
categories.lead: Use detected software as an inventory clue. Fingerprints and reported versions are not proof of a vulnerability.

templates.title: Selected product in a network
templates.note: Find a detected product within a CIDR range.
templates.tip: Compare the banner with your asset inventory.

templates.title: Selected product by hostname
templates.note: Find a product on matching hostnames.
templates.tip: Some services do not expose a detectable product.

templates.title: Selected product by organisation
templates.note: Combine provider metadata and software identification.
templates.tip: Organisation labels can include shared infrastructure.

templates.title: Selected product by ASN
templates.note: Review product matches within an autonomous system.
templates.tip: Check ownership before following up a result.

templates.title: Apache servers
templates.note: Find banners identified as Apache.
templates.tip: A product filter is more specific than a bare banner word.

templates.title: Detected WordPress component
templates.note: Find sites with a detected WordPress component.
templates.tip: A component fingerprint can be incomplete or outdated.

categories.title: Evidence & follow-up
categories.lead: Use these views to interpret results and make a focused review list.

templates.title: Results with screenshots
templates.note: Find results with captured images.
templates.tip: Treat captured content as potentially sensitive; account access applies.

templates.title: IPv6-associated results
templates.note: Find results carrying IPv6 information.
templates.tip: Review IPv6 exposure alongside your IPv4 inventory.

templates.title: Exclude empty banners
templates.note: Keep results with a non-empty main banner.
templates.tip: An empty banner does not mean a service is closed.

templates.title: HSTS header text
templates.note: Look for the HSTS header in service banner text.
templates.tip: A text match alone does not validate the whole HTTPS configuration.

templates.title: DNS port inventory
templates.note: Review indexed services on the DNS port.
templates.tip: This does not prove open recursion or amplification.

templates.title: Mail port inventory
templates.note: Review common mail-service ports.
templates.tip: Inspect the protocol and transport details in each banner.

operators.note: A matching hostname is not proof of ownership.

operators.description: Limit results to an IP range.
operators.note: Use a CIDR range you intend to review.
A reported version is not a vulnerability verdict.
Not every result has an OS fingerprint.
Viewing images can require additional account access.
Place the minus directly before the filter.

operators.description: Match alternative values in a filter.
operators.note: Use service-specific syntax instead of Google-style OR groups.

patterns.title: Scope first, narrow second
patterns.description: Pair a network boundary with the service you want to review.

patterns.title: Combine metadata
patterns.description: Require both organisation and geography to match.

patterns.title: Choose alternative ports
patterns.description: Use a comma list for either of two ports.

patterns.title: Exclude the ordinary case
patterns.description: Review SSH-related results outside the default port.

patterns.title: Separate a fingerprint from a word
patterns.description: Use product for identification and raw text for banner contents.

patterns.title: Require a readable banner
patterns.description: Remove empty banners from a scoped inventory.

guide.title: Choose a boundary
guide.text: Start with an agreed network range or known hostname. Hostname, organisation and certificate matches are discovery clues; none independently proves asset ownership.

guide.title: Read one banner
guide.text: A result describes an observed service. Check its IP, port, timestamp and protocol before broadening the query. Missing results do not establish that an asset is absent.

guide.title: Add one filter at a time
guide.text: Keep a broad baseline and compare counts as you add filters. Bare words search the main banner; use explicit filters when you mean a specific metadata field.

guide.title: Account for observation time
guide.text: Shodan’s standard search uses a recent observation window, not a live check. Recheck your own infrastructure before treating an old banner as a current finding.

guide.title: Open the right view
guide.text: The search page, Maps and Images provide different views of Shodan data. Maps and Images require membership. Shodanify only creates links and never requests a scan.

guide.title: Keep access limits visible
guide.text: Your Shodan account controls result access. Restricted tag and vuln filters require higher plans. This catalog avoids those filters; exporting data or using an API can consume credits.
